svg.title: Small Business Windows Infrastructure Lab - network diagram
svg.desc: A Linux host runs two QEMU/KVM virtual machines, DC01 (Windows Server 2025: AD DS, DNS, file shares, backup) and CL01 (Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC 2024, domain member), connected only by an isolated layer-2 lab LAN 10.10.50.0/24 with no gateway or Internet. Management uses local Unix sockets (QMP and the QEMU guest agent), not the network.
svg.text: Small Business Windows Infrastructure Lab · network
Linux host · Ubuntu 26.04 LTS · QEMU/KVM 10.2.1 run as an unprivileged user (no root, no libvirt)
DC01 · Windows Server 2025 Standard Eval · Server Core

g.text: 10.10.50.10/24 · 2 vCPU · 1.5 GB RAM · UEFI Secure Boot
DNS: AD-integrated zone, the clients' only resolver
Windows Server Backup: file-level job to E:
Disks: C: OS 60 GB · D: Data 20 GB · E: Backup 20 GB
All roles on one VM: fine for a lab, a single point of failure in production
GPO: SB-U-DepartmentDriveMaps maps F: or O:
Hardening: LLMNR and NetBIOS off (DNS only)
Users: synthetic Finance and Operations staff
Used for the onboarding and DNS-incident tickets

svg.text: Layer-2 link that exists only between the two QEMU processes (dgram over Unix sockets) · no gateway · no DHCP · no Internet
Management plane (local Unix sockets, not a network)

g.text: host/vm.sh starts each VM as a systemd --user unit · host/labctl.py talks QMP: power, screenshots, keyboard input
QEMU guest agent over virtio-serial: runs the PowerShell scripts as LocalSystem, copies files in and out
Console: VNC bound to 127.0.0.1 only, or a GTK window

svg.text: × Host Wi-Fi, home LAN and Internet: no TAP, bridge, NAT or route into the lab LAN
